questions.text: How does the lesson distinguish context from memory?

options.text: Context lasts across conversations, while memory lasts only within a single one.
Context is what the model holds during one conversation; memory retains information across conversations and over time.
They are two names for the same feature.
Memory is available only to developers, not to ordinary users.

questions.explanation: Context works like working memory within a single conversation and is lost when it ends. Memory goes a step further, carrying preferences, working style and goals into future interactions.

questions.text: Artificial General Intelligence already exists in today's most advanced AI tools.
questions.explanation: The lesson states that AGI does not exist yet, that everything in use today is narrow AI, and that there is no consensus on when — or whether — AGI will be achieved.

questions.text: Which caveats about AI memory does the lesson list?

options.text: It is selective — the system does not remember everything.
It is technically limited in how much can be stored and for how long.
It is manageable — you can view, edit and delete what the AI remembers about you.
Once stored, a memory is permanent and cannot be changed by the user.
It can be wrong — the AI may remember something incorrectly or apply it in the wrong context.

questions.explanation: Memory is described as selective, technically limited, manageable and fallible — and the fact that you can view, edit and delete it is highlighted as important for privacy.

questions.text: How does the lesson describe ASI (Artificial Superintelligence)?

options.text: A system already in use at some universities.
A hypothetical system that would significantly surpass human intelligence, belonging to theoretical discussion.
Another name for a multimodal model.
The next scheduled version of ChatGPT.

questions.explanation: ASI is presented as a speculative concept — an AI smarter than any human at everything — with no bearing on the tools teachers will use in the foreseeable future.
